body:
The maintainer asked for this work, in his own words (2026-11-18):

> Add a GPU shader issue and that is for voxel simulation..

It belongs to the GPU shader group: #2525 (nesting) and #2526 (toolpath generation).

## Question

Can a compute shader (wgpu) run the stock simulation on a voxel grid? The CPU path today is the dexel column engine. Issue #26 plans to retire it.

## Open questions for the research

1. Grid design: dense voxel grid, sparse bricks, or dexel columns on the GPU. Memory per cut volume at the stock sizes that users load. Resolution against the tolerance of the setup.
2. Material removal: a swept tool volume (cylinder, ball, bull-nose, tapered tools from the tool library) removed from the grid in one dispatch for each move or batch of moves. Accuracy at arcs and at 4-axis and 5-axis moves.
3. Read-back: a gouge, collision or rest-material result that must block the post needs the data on the CPU. State the cost and the method (async read-back, a compare against the model, a reduction in the shader).
4. Display: render the grid directly (ray march or surface extraction) without a copy to the CPU. Frame target under 10 ms (see the precalc and cache rule).
5. Backends: wgpu on Vulkan, Metal, DX12 and the browser (WebGPU). Compute support on wasm. A CPU fallback for a machine with no usable GPU. Reference #2424 (a driver freeze on one Radeon): a GPU path needs a timeout guard and a safe fallback.
6. Determinism and trust: the CPU result and the GPU result must agree within a stated tolerance. A GPU result that is wrong gives a silent wrong answer. Name the test that proves agreement (golden grids, a CPU reference).
7. Relation to `camcraft-sim`, to the stand-alone simulator (#2574 sub-issues) and to rest-material for the Adaptive and Pocket operations.

## Done means

- The research answers each question in an issue comment, with sources (published literature only; clean-room rule).
- A recommendation: build, build in part, or do not build, with a measured or cited basis.
- Sub-issues for each accepted slice, each with one `P*`, one `effort:*` and `area:*` labels, and linked under this issue.
- Then this umbrella issue is closed (`issue-claims` skill, research steps).
